title: Elicit Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs and Usage Limits
summary: Elicit pricing spans free and paid tiers for AI research assistance. See which plan fits your team's budget and research workflows.
body_markdown:
## Frequently asked questions


Before you pay, settle the five questions below, because each decides whether your cutoff date stays predictable. Where I couldn't confirm a detail, I say so rather than guess, and every answer points back to Elicit's own pages, which are the final word.


### Is Elicit free to use?


Yes, Elicit has offered a free plan you can start on without a card.


That makes it a fair way to test your real workflow, but the free allowance is the one most likely to run out mid-review, so run a realistic batch of papers before you trust it for a full project.


The limits are listed on Elicit's pricing page.


### Does Elicit offer a discount for annual billing or students?


Annual billing is the usual place for a saving, and Elicit's pricing page is where you toggle between billing periods and see the difference for yourself.


I couldn't confirm a student or academic discount. If you're at a university, ask Elicit's support before paying full price. The worst answer is no.


### Can I cancel Elicit or downgrade mid-month?


I couldn't confirm the exact terms. Whether a downgrade takes effect immediately or at the end of the billing period decides whether you pay for capacity you no longer need.


So read the billing section of your account settings and Elicit's terms before you commit, especially on an annual plan.


### Does Elicit have team or enterprise pricing?


Elicit's pricing page lists plans beyond the individual ones, and larger organizations are generally handled by contacting Elicit directly.


If you're three people sharing one review, price the team option against separate individual plans, since shared limits are what you're really buying.


### Do unused Elicit credits or allowances roll over?


Don't assume they do. Most usage allowances are built to reset on a cycle, so work you leave undone can simply vanish.


Check how Elicit describes your plan's allowance on the pricing page, then schedule the heavy extraction work early in the cycle rather than saving it for the end.
